metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to find electric cars on cars.com with price/distance/zip filters. cars.com was blocked by Cloudflare. The agent opened a new tab (step 4, action=left_click on new tab button) to try accessing Google as a workaround.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open a new tab in Chrome by clicking the new tab button or pressing Ctrl+T. The agent demonstrated this at step 4 of the trajectory.
metadata.failure_analysis: cars.com was blocked by Cloudflare. The agent's tab-opening action (step 4) was part of a workaround attempt that still failed due to the site block.
metadata.task_rationale: Targets the tab-opening sub-skill demonstrated around step 4. The evaluator counts open tabs; the initial state has 1 tab so it will not pass.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening at least one new tab in Chrome. Evaluator uses custom check_new_tab_opened metric which verifies at least 2 tabs are open via open_tabs_info getter. Initial state has 1 tab (cars.com blocked) so it does not pass.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'open_tabs_info' correctly extracts the list of open tabs via Chrome DevTools Protocol, returning [{title, url}] dicts — the right state to count open tabs.

Metric 'check_new_tab_opened' correctly handles the 'type: rule' parameter pattern: expected IS the rules dict ({min_tabs: 2}), and the metric directly calls expected.get('min_tabs', 2) — no incorrect expected.get('rules', ...) wrapping.
Logic 'len(result) >= min_tabs' is semantically correct: if a new tab was opened from an initial state of 1 tab, at least 2 tabs will be present.
Initial state sets up 1 tab (cars.com), so the evaluator will correctly return 0.0 for a do-nothing agent — good negative-control resistance.
No postconfig is needed since tab count is a live browser state read via CDP and does not depend on any closed UI dialog.
Non-list result guard (isinstance check) handles edge cases such as CDP connection failure gracefully.
